title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations: catch up with an old friend, chat at a family dinner, argue about where to go and reach a compromise, and plan a trip together — linking your ideas in long sentences and switching between ته and تاسو as people come and go.
intro:
This last unit puts everything together. Real conversations are long and messy: you catch up on years of news, you're interrupted by an aunt with more food, the cousins argue about Bamiyan versus Paghman, grandpa wakes up and has an opinion, and in the end somebody's mother settles it.

Two skills make that possible. **Linking**: 'although …', 'not only … but also …', 'instead of …', 'despite …', 'that's why …'. And **switching register**: ته with your cousin, تاسو with your grandfather, the same evening, sometimes in the same sentence.

grammar.title: Linking long sentences
grammar.body:
Short sentences joined with او and خو (unit 14) get you started. To sound fluent you need connectors that show **how** two ideas relate.

**Although: که څه هم …، خو …** Pashto likes to mark both halves: **که څه هم** ستړی وم، **خو** درغلم 'although I was tired, I came'. The more formal **سره له دې چې** works the same way.

**Not only … but also: نه يوازې …، بلکې … هم**: **نه يوازې** ارزان دی، **بلکې** ښکلی **هم** دی. On its own, **بلکې** means 'but rather', correcting a negative: زه ښار نه، **بلکې** طبيعت غواړم 'I don't want the city but nature'.

**Instead of: د X پر ځای**: **د** فلم **پر ځای** بهر لاړ شو 'let's go out instead of watching a film'. With a verb, use the infinitive: د ناستې **پر ځای** 'instead of sitting'.

**That's why: له همدې امله** (or casual **نو ځکه**) starts the result: موټر مې خراب و، **له همدې امله** ناوخته شوم.

**Also useful:** **ځکه چې** 'because' (unit 14), **د دې لپاره چې** + subjunctive 'so that', **يا … يا …** 'either … or', **نه … نه …** 'neither … nor', **که نه** 'otherwise' (unit 19), **کله چې / تر څو چې** 'when / until' (unit 30).

**The trap:** don't drop خو after که څه هم in speech — without it the sentence sounds unfinished to a Pashtun ear.

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
At a family dinner you will talk to five people in three registers within a minute. The switches are small but everyone notices them.

**1. ته or تاسو.** Use **ته** with friends, cousins, younger siblings and children; most people also use ته with their own mother (and many with their father). Use **تاسو** with grandparents, uncles and aunts, parents-in-law, older neighbours, and anyone you've just met. The verb follows: ته وخوره / تاسو **وخورئ**؛ ته ستړی **يې** / تاسو ستړي **ياست** (with تاسو the adjective goes into the plural).

**2. Titles instead of names.** Never call an older relative by their bare name: say **بابا**، **ادې**، **کاکا**، **ترور**، **لالا**، **خور جانې**. Add **جان / جانه** for warmth: بابا **جانه**.

**3. Respectful plural about elders.** When you talk **about** a grandparent or an older relative, Pashtuns often use the **plural** verb: بابا مو ويده **دي** 'your grandpa is asleep', کاکا راغلي **دي** 'uncle has come'. It sounds natural and kind; the singular is not rude, just plainer.

**4. Softening with elders.** Add **مهرباني وکړئ**, **که اجازه وي** 'if you'll allow', and avoid **چوپ شه** or **ضد مه کوه** — the same idea to an elder is **لږ صبر وکړئ** 'please wait a moment'.

**The trap:** switch the whole sentence, not half of it. تاسو … وخوره (polite pronoun, informal verb) sounds clumsy; say **تاسو … وخورئ**.

examples.native: وروره، ته هم وخوره. کاکا، تاسو هم وخورئ.

dialogue.title: Bamiyan or Paghman?
dialogue.setting: Eid is next week. After dinner at the family home in Kabul, the cousins Zalmay and Sana argue about where to go; their grandfather (Baba) is dozing on the cushions and Sana's mother is pouring tea.

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: ثنا، ګوره، د اختر لپاره مې يو عالي پلان جوړ کړی: باميان!
lines.roman: sanā́, góra, də axtár lapā́ra me yaw ālí plān joṛ kaṛáy: bāmiyā́n!
lines.en: Sana, look, I've got a brilliant plan for Eid: Bamiyan!

lines.native: باميان؟ که څه هم ښکلی دی، خو ډېر لرې دی. ولې نه پغمان؟
lines.roman: bāmiyā́n? ka tsə ham ṣkə́lay day, xo ḍer lə́re day. wə́le na paġmā́n?
lines.en: Bamiyan? It's beautiful, sure, but it's really far. Why not Paghman?

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: پغمان؟ هلته خو هر کال ځو! زه پغمان نه، بلکې يو رښتينی سفر غواړم.
lines.roman: paġmā́n? hálta xo har kāl dzu! zə paġmā́n na, bálke yaw rəṣtináy safár ġwā́ṛəm.
lines.en: Paghman? We go there every year! I don't want Paghman, I want a real trip.

lines.speaker: Sana
lines.native: ضد مه کوه! د باميان لګښت به څومره وي؟
lines.roman: zid ma kawa! də bāmiyā́n lagə́ṣt ba tsómra wi?
lines.en: Don't be stubborn! And how much would Bamiyan cost?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: بچيو، لږ ورو، بابا مو ويده دي.
lines.roman: bachíyo, ləẓ wro, bābā́ mo widə́ di.
lines.en: Kids, keep it down — your grandpa's asleep.

lines.speaker: Baba
lines.native: نه، ويښ يم، ويښ يم. څه خبره ده؟
lines.roman: na, wiṣ yəm, wiṣ yəm. tsə xabə́ra da?
lines.en: No, I'm awake, I'm awake. What's going on?

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: بابا جانه، بښنه غواړم. د اختر د سفر خبره مو کوله. تاسو باميان ليدلی دی؟
lines.roman: bābā́ jā́na, baṣə́na ġwā́ṛəm. də axtár də safár xabə́ra mo kawə́la. tāso bāmiyā́n lidə́lay day?
lines.en: Grandpa, sorry. We were talking about an Eid trip. Have you ever seen Bamiyan?

lines.speaker: Baba
lines.native: هو، پنځوس کاله مخکې. هغه وخت سفر ډېر سخت و، دوه ورځې په لار وو.
lines.roman: ho, pindzós kā́la mə́xke. haġá waxt safár ḍer saxt wə, dwa wradzé pə lār wu.
lines.en: Yes, fifty years ago. Travelling was really hard then — we were on the road for two days.

lines.speaker: Sana
lines.native: بابا، که تاسو هم راشئ، زه به باميان ته هم ځم!
lines.roman: bābā́, ka tāso ham rā́shəy, zə ba bāmiyā́n ta ham dzəm!
lines.en: Grandpa, if you come too, I'll even go to Bamiyan!

lines.speaker: Baba
lines.native: زه زوړ يم، لورې. خو د پغمان ډنډ ته به درسره لاړ شم.
lines.roman: zə zoṛ yəm, lúre. xo də paġmā́n ḍanḍ ta ba dərsara lāṛ shəm.
lines.en: I'm old, my girl. But I'll come with you to the lake at Paghman.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: نو جوړجاړی وشو: لومړی له بابا سره پغمان، او بيا دې ځوانان باميان ته لاړ شي.
lines.roman: no joṛjā́ṛay wə́shu: lumṛáy la bābā́ sara paġmā́n, aw biyā́ de dzwānā́n bāmiyā́n ta lāṛ shi.
lines.en: So that's settled: first Paghman with Grandpa, and then the young ones can go to Bamiyan.

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: واه ادې! ته خو د جرګې مشره يې!
lines.roman: wāh adé! tə xo də jərgé məshə́ra ye!
lines.en: Wow, Mum! You're the head of the jirga!

lines.speaker: Baba
lines.native: په هر صورت، زما رايه هم ورسره ده. اوس چای راوړئ!
lines.roman: pə har surát, zmā rāyá ham wərsara da. os chāy rā́wṛəy!
lines.en: Either way, my vote's with her. Now bring the tea!

culture:
A real Pashtun conversation starts slowly. Before any news, there is a round of **ستړي مه شې**, **څه حال دی؟**, **کور کې ټول ښه دي؟**, **ماشومان دې روغ دي؟** — asking after every member of the family, sometimes by name. Rushing straight to business sounds cold; take your time and ask back.

At family gatherings the oldest person present has the last word, and young people show respect by switching to تاسو, using titles like **بابا** and **کاکا**, standing up when an elder comes in, and not contradicting them directly — disagree with **که اجازه وي …** or through a parent. Talking *about* elders in the plural (بابا مو ويده دي) is a small sign of respect that everyone notices.

Group decisions — where to go on **اختر**, who brings what — are made over tea and can take a while; a joke and a compromise (**جوړجاړی**) usually end them. Congratulations: you can now catch up with an old friend, sit through a family dinner, and argue your way to Bamiyan in Pashto. **بريالی اوسې!**

lessons.title: Catching up with an old friend

tip.title: Catching up, Pashtun style
tip.body:
- Start with the full round: **ستړی مه شې**، **څه حال دی؟**، **کور کې ټول ښه دي؟**
- Then the news: **نور څه نوي خبرونه؟**، **واده دې وکړ؟**
- Leave warmly: **بيا به سره وګورو**، **خدای پامان**.

new: ستړی مه شې! ډېر وخت وشو، چېرته وې؟
څه حال دی؟ ټول ښه دي؟
ښه، نو اوس ځم، بيا به سره وګورو.

tip.title: Linking ideas
tip.body:
- **که څه هم** …، **خو** … 'although': keep the خو.
- **نه يوازې** …، **بلکې** … **هم** 'not only … but also'.
- **د** X **پر ځای** 'instead of X'.
- **له همدې امله** 'that's why'.
tip.pattern: که څه هم …، خو … · د … پر ځای

tip.title: ته or تاسو — switch the whole sentence
tip.body:
- Cousins, friends, mum: **ته** + -a verbs (وخوره، کېنه).
- Grandparents, uncles, elders: **تاسو** + -əy verbs (وخورئ، کېنئ), plural adjectives (ستړي ياست).
- Titles, not names: **بابا**، **ادې**، **کاکا** + جانه.
- About elders, often the plural: بابا ويده **دي**.

sentences.en: Mum, why aren't you eating?

sentences.native: د اختر په رخصتيو کې چېرته سېل ته ځو؟
sentences.roman: də axtár pə ruxsatíyo ke chérta sel ta dzu?
sentences.en: Where shall we go for a day out over the Eid holidays?

sentences.native: د قرغې ډنډ ته ځو؟
sentences.roman: də qarġé ḍanḍ ta dzu?
sentences.en: Shall we go to Qargha lake?

sentences.native: هلته طبيعت ډېر ښکلی دی.
sentences.roman: hálta tabiʿát ḍer ṣkə́lay day.
sentences.en: The countryside there is really beautiful.

sentences.native: د پغمان ښکلا په پسرلي کې بل شان وي.
sentences.roman: də paġmā́n ṣkulā́ pə psarlí ke bəl shān wi.
sentences.en: Paghman is something else in spring.

sentences.native: زموږ لومړی منزل جلال اباد دی.
sentences.roman: zmuẓ lumṛáy manzə́l jalāl ābā́d day.
sentences.en: Our first stop is Jalalabad.

sentences.native: منزل ته څو ساعته لار ده؟
sentences.roman: manzə́l ta tso sāʿáta lār da?
sentences.en: How many hours is it to where we're going?

sentences.native: زه ښار نه، بلکې طبيعت غواړم.
sentences.roman: zə ṣār na, bálke tabiʿát ġwā́ṛəm.
sentences.en: I don't want a city — I want nature.

sentences.native: که څه هم لرې دی، خو ارزښت لري.
sentences.roman: ka tsə ham lə́re day, xo arzə́ṣt lári.
sentences.en: It's far, but it's worth it.

sentences.native: ډنډ ته نږدې يو ښه هوټل شته.
sentences.roman: ḍanḍ ta nəẓdé yaw ṣə hoṭál shta.
sentences.en: There's a nice restaurant near the lake.

sentences.native: ته تل ضد کوې!
sentences.roman: tə tal zid kawé!
sentences.en: You're always so stubborn!

sentences.native: ضد نه کوم، يوازې خپل نظر وايم.
sentences.roman: zid na kawə́m, yawā́ze xpəl nazár wā́yəm.
sentences.en: I'm not being stubborn, I'm just giving my opinion.

sentences.native: هر څوک دې خپله رايه ووايي.
sentences.roman: har tsok de xpə́la rāyá wə́wāyi.
sentences.en: Everyone say what they want.

sentences.native: اکثريت غر ته تلل غواړي.
sentences.roman: aksariyát ġar ta tlə́l ġwā́ṛi.
sentences.en: Most people want to go to the mountains.

sentences.native: که اکثريت داسې وايي، نو سمه ده.
sentences.roman: ka aksariyát dā́se wā́yi, no sáma da.
sentences.en: If that's what most people want, fine.

sentences.native: راځئ جوړجاړی وکړو: يوه ورځ غر، يوه ورځ ډنډ.
sentences.roman: rā́dzəy joṛjā́ṛay wə́kṛu: yáwa wradz ġar, yáwa wradz ḍanḍ.
sentences.en: Let's compromise: one day the mountains, one day the lake.

sentences.native: دا ښه جوړجاړی دی، زه موافق يم.
sentences.roman: dā ṣə joṛjā́ṛay day, zə muwāfíq yəm.
sentences.en: That's a good deal — I agree.

sentences.native: په هر صورت، زه به ستاسو سره يم.
sentences.roman: pə har surát, zə ba stāso sara yəm.
sentences.en: Either way, I'll be with you.

sentences.native: زما رايه د ډنډ لپاره ده.
sentences.roman: zmā rāyá də ḍanḍ lapā́ra da.
sentences.en: My vote's for the lake.

lessons.title: Planning the trip
new: خواړه زه راوړم، ته موټر تيار کړه.

sentences.native: د سفر لګښت به نيم نيم کوو.
sentences.roman: də safár lagə́ṣt ba nim nim kawú.
sentences.en: We'll split the cost of the trip.

sentences.native: که په بس کې لاړ شو، لګښت به کم وي.
sentences.roman: ka pə bas ke lāṛ shu, lagə́ṣt ba kam wi.
sentences.en: If we go by bus, it'll cost less.

sentences.native: خيمه لرو که هوټل ته ځو؟
sentences.roman: xaymá láru ka hoṭál ta dzu?
sentences.en: Have we got a tent, or are we going to a hotel?

sentences.native: زما سره يوه لويه خيمه شته.
sentences.roman: zmā sara yáwa lóya xaymá shta.
sentences.en: I've got a big tent.

sentences.native: سهار وختي ووځو چې ګرمي نه وي.
sentences.roman: sahā́r waxtí wə́wudzu che garmí na wi.
sentences.en: Let's leave early in the morning so it's not too hot.

sentences.native: خواړه دې مه هېروه!
sentences.roman: xwāṛə́ de ma herawa!
sentences.en: Don't forget the food!

sentences.native: د هر څه لګښت راته وليکه.
sentences.roman: də har tsə lagə́ṣt rā́ta wə́lika.
sentences.en: Write down the cost of everything for me.

sentences.native: خيمه دې په موټر کې کېښوده؟
sentences.roman: xaymá de pə moṭár ke kéṣoda?
sentences.en: Did you put the tent in the car?

sentences.native: ټول تيار ياست؟ هله، ځو!
sentences.roman: ṭol tayā́r yāst? hála, dzu!
sentences.en: Everyone ready? Come on, let's go!
